title: Private On‑Prem Activation Velocity Framework & Quarterly Cadence
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Define and roll out an activation velocity framework for private (VPC/on‑prem) customers that maps sprint-level throughput targets to customer enablement milestones, test/compatibility automation, and OKR metrics. Goal is to increase safe tenant activation capacity by 3x while reducing manual gating work and regression risk. Scope includes playbooks, gating automation, capacity planning templates, and a lightweight preflight compatibility harness integrated with onboarding CI.
background: We are seeing longer lead times and mismatch between engineering capacity and customer readiness for private/on‑prem activations. Current process relies on ad‑hoc scripts and manual validation during each wave. This slows commercial rollouts and increases failure budget use. The framework will standardize signals and handoffs between Sales/CS, Solutions, Eng-Delivery, and SRE, and connects those signals to OKR tracking for the quarter.
acceptance_criteria: A standardized activation checklist (runbook) published and reviewed by Eng, SRE, Solutions, and Legal
A preflight compatibility harness that runs core smoke checks against a sample on‑prem staging cluster (automated) and returns pass/fail with logs
Sprint throughput model: template that converts engineering story points + infra capacity into expected activation throughput (tenants/week), validated with two pilot customers
OKR alignment doc showing how velocity metrics feed into the quarter OKR and success metrics (activation rate, MTTR for activation failures, manual validation hours per activation)
Integration points documented: onboarding CI job, customer readiness score in onboarding dashboard, and ownership matrix for rollouts
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Solutions Engineering, Sales Ops. Agreed owners and 6‑week pilot scope (2 pilot customers). Action: SRE to prototype preflight harness by Feb 26.

2026-02-18: Completed first draft of activation checklist. UX/Console PM provided feedback to expose 'readiness score' in tenant dashboard. Added item to include KMS/HSM validation step for high‑security customers.

2026-02-24: Engineering flagged risk: existing staging images do not reproduce onprem networking constraints. Tradeoff discussion: add network emulation vs limit pilot to customers with flexible networks. Decided to add minimal network checks for pilot and schedule network emulation work as dependency.

2026-03-01: Pilot customer enrollment confirmed (AcmeBio, Finex Labs). SRE prototype harness run against AcmeBio dev cluster — initial pass with 2 known exceptions (TLS cipher mismatch, kernel module). Logged as ENG-83021 and ENG-83022. Next: remediation plan and rerun preflight.
decisions: Ship a lightweight, opinionated preflight harness first (smoke tests + KV cache warmup + KMS handshake) rather than a full fidelity emulator to reduce scope and unblock pilots.
Expose a single ‘customer readiness score’ in the Console tenant view (0–100) derived from checklist pass rates and automated preflight results.
Require security review for customers opting into HSM/KMS validations; default pilot will skip hardware-backed tests until SRE confirms processes.
notes: Next steps: finalize preflight harness MVP by 2026-03-15, onboard first pilot customer, collect telemetry for 2 sprints, and present quarter OKR mapping to GTM on 2026-03-22. If pilot shows >60% automated pass rate, scale to wave 1; otherwise iterate on automation and visibility.
